questions.stem: The IUPAC name of the compound CH3-CH2-CH2-OH is:

options.option_text: Propan-1-ol — 3-carbon chain (prop), single bond (an), hydroxyl at position 1 (-1-ol)
Propanal — propanal has an aldehyde group (-CHO), not a hydroxyl group (-OH)
Propanone — propanone is the IUPAC name of acetone, which has a ketone group
Propanoic acid — propanoic acid has a carboxyl group (-COOH), not a hydroxyl group

questions.explanation: IUPAC NAMING: (1) Find longest chain = 3 carbons = PROP. (2) All single bonds = -AN. (3) Functional group: -OH = -OL. (4) Position: OH at carbon 1 = -1-. FULL NAME: PROPAN-1-OL. COMMON NAME: n-propanol or 1-propanol. FUNCTIONAL GROUP TABLE: -OH = alcohol (-ol); -CHO = aldehyde (-al); C=O middle = ketone (-one); -COOH = carboxylic acid (-oic acid); -NH2 = amine (-amine). PYQ: IUPAC naming of simple organic compounds in SSC CGL, IBPS PO chemistry — 1x per cycle.

questions.stem: Alkanes, alkenes, and alkynes are all hydrocarbons. Which series contains a carbon-carbon triple bond?

options.option_text: Alkynes — general formula CnH(2n-2); contain at least one C≡C triple bond
Alkanes — saturated hydrocarbons; contain only C-C single bonds and no double or triple bonds
Alkenes — contain one C=C double bond; general formula CnH(2n), not triple bond
Arenes — aromatic hydrocarbons with delocalised pi electrons; benzene ring, not triple bond

questions.explanation: HYDROCARBON SERIES: ALKANE: C-C single bond only. Formula: CnH(2n+2). SATURATED. Examples: methane, ethane, propane. ALKENE: C=C double bond. Formula: CnH(2n). UNSATURATED. Examples: ethene, propene. ALKYNE: C≡C triple bond. Formula: CnH(2n-2). MOST UNSATURATED. Examples: ethyne (acetylene, C2H2). DEGREE OF UNSATURATION: 1 double bond = 1 degree; 1 triple bond = 2 degrees; 1 ring = 1 degree. INDUSTRIAL: acetylene (ethyne) used in welding (oxy-acetylene torch). PYQ: alkane/alkene/alkyne series — SSC CGL, IBPS PO chemistry standard 1-marker.

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs are structural isomers (same molecular formula, different structural arrangement)?

options.option_text: Ethanol (CH3CH2OH) and dimethyl ether (CH3-O-CH3) — both have formula C2H6O
Methane (CH4) and ethane (C2H6) — different molecular formulas; these are homologues, not isomers
Butane (C4H10) and pentane (C5H12) — different molecular formulas; consecutive homologues
Water (H2O) and hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) — different molecular formulas; not isomers of any type

questions.explanation: STRUCTURAL ISOMERS: same molecular formula, different structural arrangements. Ethanol: C2H6O with -OH group (alcohol). Dimethyl ether: C2H6O with C-O-C linkage (ether). BOTH = C2H6O but completely different structures and properties. HOMOLOGUES: compounds in the same series that differ by CH2 (like methane/ethane). CHAIN ISOMERS: same formula, different carbon chain (butane vs isobutane = both C4H10). POSITIONAL ISOMERS: same formula, same chain, functional group at different position (propan-1-ol vs propan-2-ol = both C3H8O). PYQ: structural isomerism + ethanol/ether pair in SSC CGL, IBPS PO chemistry.

questions.stem: The reaction of ethene (CH2=CH2) with HBr to form bromoethane (CH3CH2Br) is an example of:

options.option_text: Addition reaction — a molecule (HBr) adds across the C=C double bond without removing any atoms
Substitution reaction — substitution replaces one atom; but here nothing is removed from ethene
Elimination reaction — elimination removes atoms to form a double bond; the opposite of addition
Combustion reaction — combustion requires oxygen and produces CO2 and H2O only

questions.explanation: ADDITION REACTION: occurs across a double or triple bond. No atoms are lost; the molecule grows. CH2=CH2 + HBr → CH3CH2Br. The pi bond in C=C breaks; H adds to one carbon, Br adds to the other. MARKOVNIKOV'S RULE: H adds to the carbon with MORE H atoms (for asymmetric alkenes). SUBSTITUTION: one atom/group replaced by another (e.g., alkane + Cl2 → chloroalkane + HCl). ELIMINATION: removal of atoms from adjacent carbons to form C=C (reverse of addition). HYDROGENATION: addition of H2 across C=C (used to harden oils into fats). PYQ: addition vs substitution reaction distinction in SSC CGL, IBPS PO, UPSC chemistry.

questions.stem: Fermentation of glucose by yeast produces ethanol and carbon dioxide. The type of reaction occurring is:

options.option_text: Anaerobic respiration (biochemical reduction) — yeast breaks down glucose without oxygen
Aerobic combustion — combustion requires oxygen and produces only CO2 and H2O; not ethanol
Esterification — esterification combines an alcohol with an acid to form an ester and water
Saponification — saponification is the hydrolysis of fats/oils with alkali to form soap

questions.explanation: FERMENTATION: C6H12O6 → 2C2H5OH + 2CO2. Catalysed by zymase enzyme in yeast. CONDITIONS: anaerobic (no oxygen), temperature 30-35°C. INDUSTRIAL USE: brewing beer, wine, spirits; bread making (CO2 causes dough to rise). BIOETHANOL: fermentation of sugarcane/corn for fuel. LIMITATIONS: maximum ethanol concentration ~15% (above this yeast dies). DISTILLATION: used to concentrate ethanol beyond 15%. VINEGAR: ethanol oxidised to acetic acid by Acetobacter bacteria. PYQ: fermentation reaction + products in SSC CGL, IBPS PO, UPSC science GK.

questions.stem: A compound with molecular formula C4H8O shows a carbonyl group (C=O) in the middle of the chain, not at the end. Its IUPAC name is:

options.option_text: Butan-2-one (methyl ethyl ketone) — 4C chain, C=O at position 2, no H on carbonyl carbon
Butanal — butanal has a -CHO (aldehyde) at the end of the chain, not the middle
But-2-ene — but-2-ene has a C=C double bond, not a C=O carbonyl group
Butanoic acid — butanoic acid has a -COOH carboxyl group, not a simple ketone C=O

questions.explanation: KETONE: C=O carbonyl group flanked by two carbon groups (not hydrogen). When C=O is in the MIDDLE of the chain, the compound is a KETONE (-one). BUTAN-2-ONE: CH3-CO-CH2-CH3. 4-carbon chain (but), C=O at position 2 (-2-), ketone suffix (-one). COMMON NAME: methyl ethyl ketone (MEK) — used as industrial solvent. DISTINCTION: ALDEHYDE has C=O at the END of the chain (-CHO); KETONE has C=O in the MIDDLE. Butan-2-one (C4H8O) is a positional isomer of butanal (C4H8O) — same formula, different position of C=O. PYQ: aldehyde vs ketone identification in SSC CGL, IBPS PO chemistry.

questions.stem: Benzene (C6H6) undergoes substitution reactions rather than addition reactions, despite having three apparent double bonds. This is because:

options.option_text: Benzene's pi electrons are delocalised over all 6 carbons, giving it aromatic stability that addition would destroy
Benzene has no double bonds; all C-C bonds in benzene are single bonds of equal length (not this)
Benzene undergoes addition because it has double bonds; substitution is observed only occasionally
Benzene is too unreactive to undergo any reactions under normal laboratory conditions (not this)

questions.explanation: BENZENE AROMATICITY: the 6 pi electrons are delocalised in a ring above and below the carbon plane (resonance). ALL C-C BONDS ARE EQUAL LENGTH (1.40 Å — between single 1.54 Å and double 1.34 Å). HUCKEL'S RULE: 4n+2 pi electrons (n=1 → 6 electrons) = aromatic. AROMATIC STABILITY: the delocalisation energy (~150 kJ/mol) makes the ring extremely stable. ADDITION would break aromaticity (gain in energy = unfavourable). SUBSTITUTION retains the aromatic ring (one H replaced, ring intact). ELECTROPHILIC AROMATIC SUBSTITUTION (EAS): nitration, halogenation, sulphonation, Friedel-Crafts alkylation/acylation. PYQ: why benzene prefers substitution in UPSC GS-1, IBPS PO advanced chemistry.
